title: What is known about 1RB0LC_0LC1RF_1LE1RD_0RC1RC_0LA1LA_---1RA
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0LC_0LC1RF_1LE1RD_0RC1RC_0LA1LA_---1RA.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: Open, and probably never halting. From step 118 the run is the orbit of an explicit map on two numbers, U(a, b) and V(a, b). The map is proved in Lean's kernel for every even a: from every event with a even, a ≥ 2 and b ≥ 1 the machine reaches the event the map gives, in exactly the steps it gives, except at the halting events (a divisible by 4, b = 1). The run from blank tape only ever has even a. Lean reduces non-halting to a statement about the map alone (not_halts_of_orbit) and checks the orbit: 3,000 passes in the kernel (no halt in 10500 steps), 105 compiled (1010000 steps). Reaching b = 1 needs b to land within a few units of a, so the chance of a halt is about 2/a, and a grows exponentially.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F0); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: The pass map for every even a
claims.text: Events: Ev .U a b = A> 011011 1^a 0 1^b and Ev .V a b = A> 1110 1^a 0 1^b. next F a b gives the next event and the exact number of steps to it; next_sound proves that the machine goes there. next_isSome: it is defined at every event with a even, a ≥ 2 and b ≥ 1 except U/V(a, 1) with a = 0 mod 4. The cases: a = 2 mod 4 with b odd (to o((3a+10)/2, b)); a = 0 mod 4 with b = 3, 5 or b ≥ 7 odd; a, b even with b ≥ a+4, b ≤ a−2, b = a or b = a+2. Each is a family with a generic part and a few small values, 32 case theorems in all, built from symbolic-simulator segments and four loops proved by induction: a round of the b-odd phase (four 1s of a become six) for each residue of a mod 4, and a round of the Euclid phase (both blocks lose 11) for each of the two orders. Axioms: propext and Quot.sound only.

claims.title: Non-halting reduces to the map; 3,000 passes checked
claims.text: init_U: blank tape reaches U(4, 3) after 118 steps. not_halts_of_orbit: if the orbit of next from U(4, 3) never gets stuck, the machine never halts. Each pass takes at least one step (next_pos), so the orbit's step count grows without bound. The kernel evaluates the first 3,000 passes: never stuck, so no halt in the first 10500 steps (no_halt_3k). Pass 34 is U(35,354, 10,986) at step 1,916,511,832, as direct simulation finds (orbit_34).

claims.title: 10<sup>5</sup> passes, no halt in 10<sup>10000</sup> steps
claims.text: The same orbit check for the first 10<sup>5</sup> passes, by compiled evaluation.

claims.title: The pass map against direct simulation, including odd a
claims.text: Sample the run when the head is in A at the left end. From step 118 the tape is U(a, b) = A> 011011 1^a 0 1^b or V(a, b) = A> 1110 1^a 0 1^b. The next such configuration is given by an explicit map with cases on a mod 4, the parity of b, and b compared with a (written out in py/emap.py): for example U(a, b) with a = 0 mod 4 and odd b ≥ 7 goes to U((3a+16)/2, b−5), and with a and b even and b ≤ a−2 to V(3b+4, a−b−1). The map was checked against direct simulation for every start with a < 60 and b < 70 (7,980 starts the map covers), 300 random starts with 15 ≤ a < 2,000, and 84 starts with small odd a and large b. The cases with odd a, which the run never reaches, are checked this way only; the even-a cases are now proved (above).

claims.title: The halting condition
claims.text: The machine halts exactly when it reaches U(a, 1) or V(a, 1) with a = 0 mod 4: the head then reads a 0 in state F. Every other U/V configuration leads to another one; for even a this half is now proved in Lean (next_isSome). That the halting events do halt was checked by simulation on the grid above.

claims.title: The map against the run from blank tape
claims.text: The 38 U/V-events of the direct run from blank tape up to 8.7·10<sup>9</sup> steps, from U(4, 3) at step 118 to U(74,180, 24,362) at step 8,744,109,161, each follow from the one before by the map.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>6</sup> passes
claims.text: Iterating the map from U(4, 3) with exact big integers gives no halt in 10<sup>6</sup> passes. Both numbers then have about 96,600 digits. 14% of the passes make a smaller (a subtraction-and-swap step), and b came down to 2 a few times, but never to 1 with a = 0 mod 4. (The first 10<sup>5</sup> of these passes are also checked in Lean, above.)

claims.title: Probviously non-halting: the chance of a halt is about 2/a
claims.text: Reaching b = 1 needs a subtraction step that leaves exactly 1, so b has to land on one of a few values next to a (b = a−2, a+4, a−7, a−13), and then a has to be divisible by 4. Iterating the map from 20,000 random starts at each scale (100,000 at S = 10⁴) S (a in [S, 2S), b in [0, 2S)) gives halting frequencies 2.0·10<sup>−2</sup>, 2.5·10<sup>−3</sup> and 2.1·10<sup>−4</sup> for S = 10<sup>2</sup>, 10<sup>3</sup> and 10<sup>4</sup>, so the frequency is about 2/S. Since a grows exponentially, this sum is dominated by its first terms. From the last simulated event (a = 74,180) the estimate is about 3·10<sup>−5</sup>, and after the 10<sup>6</sup> passes iterated it is about 10<sup>−96,600</sup>.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known, but probably not. A proof would need to show that the subtraction steps never leave exactly b = 1 with a = 0 mod 4 along this orbit: a question about the long-run residues of a 3/2-Collatz-like orbit, which is out of reach.

explainer.lede: Probably never. The tape holds two numbers side by side, a and b. Most passes multiply a by 3/2 and move b a little. Now and then the machine subtracts the smaller number from the larger one, as in Euclid's algorithm, and swaps them. It stops only if that subtraction leaves exactly b = 1 at the wrong moment, a coincidence that gets rarer as the numbers grow.

facts.text: The pass map for every even a, and its exact halting condition b = 1, a = 0 mod 4, in Lean's kernel.
No halt: the first 10<sup>5</sup> passes never reach a halting event (3,000 of them checked by the kernel alone).
Chance of a halt from size a; a grows exponentially, so the total is tiny.

sections.heading: Two numbers side by side
html: Every so often the head is in state A at the left end of the tape, and the tape is then a short word followed by two blocks of 1s, of lengths a and b, separated by one 0. The word is either 011011 (call this U(a, b)) or 1110 (V(a, b)).

One pass from such a moment to the next does one of two things. If b is odd, or a is odd and b is large, the machine multiplies a by about 3/2 (or 3) and moves b by a few units. If both are even, it subtracts the smaller number from the larger one and triples what is left on the left, swapping the two when b was the smaller: a step of Euclid's algorithm mixed with a Collatz step. The main cases, from U (V is the same with slightly different constants):

casefrom U(a, b)what it does
a = 0 mod 4, b odd ≥ 7U((3a+16)/2, b−5)a × 3/2, b down by 5
a = 2 mod 4, b oddV((3a+10)/2, b)a × 3/2
a = 1 mod 4, b oddV((3a−3)/2, b+8)a × 3/2, b up by 8
a = 3 mod 4, b oddU((3a+3)/2, b+3)a × 3/2, b up by 3
a, b even, b ≥ a+4U(3a+6, b−a−3)subtract a from b, triple a
a, b even, b ≤ a−2V(3b+4, a−b−1)subtract and swap
a odd, b even, b ≥ a−7U(3a−5, b−a+8)subtract a from b, triple a
a odd, b even, b ≤ a−13V(3b+26, a−b−12)subtract and swap
a = 0 mod 4, b = 1halt

From blank tape: U(4, 3) at step 118, then V(4, 14), V(20, 7), V(40, 2), U(10, 37), …, U(100, 7), U(158, 2), V(10, 155), …, U(74,180, 24,362) at step 8.7 billion. Both numbers keep growing, and the visited tape grows like the square root of the step count.

sections.heading: Only at b = 1
html: The machine stops exactly when it reaches U(a, 1) or V(a, 1) with a divisible by 4. The rule that lowers b by 5 makes it even, so b = 1 can only come out of a subtraction that leaves exactly 1. That needs b to land on one of a handful of values next to a: a coincidence with a chance of about 2/a.

Starting the map from random pairs of size S gives halting frequencies close to 2/S (2% at S = 100, 0.25% at 1,000, 0.021% at 10,000). Along the actual run a grows exponentially, so the total chance is dominated by the first terms. About 3·10−5 was left when direct simulation stopped, and about 10−96,600 is left after the 1,000,000 passes that were iterated.

sections.heading: The map is proved; what is left is arithmetic
html:
• Every pass is proved for even a, the only kind the run meets: Lean's kernel checks that from every U(a, b) or V(a, b) with a even the machine reaches the event the map predicts, in exactly the predicted number of steps, unless b = 1 and 4 divides a. There are 32 cases, each a few sweeps. The repeated part of a sweep (four 1s of a turned into six on the left, or both blocks shortened by two) is proved once and iterated by induction.
  • Non-halting is reduced to the map. Lean proves that if the map's orbit from U(4, 3) never reaches b = 1 with 4 dividing a, the machine never halts. It then evaluates that orbit: 3,000 passes in the kernel (more than 10500 steps) and 105 compiled (1010000 steps), none of them halting.
  • What is missing is a reason why b = 1 never comes up. That looks as hard as any Collatz question.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.057). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.492).
After 109 steps the tape spans 31,855 cells (69 left of the start, 23,551 right), with a density of 1s of 1.0.

The tape (run-length coded, 1^5 is five 1s, C>0 the head in state C on a 0) at some of the last moments the head reached a new cell, cut to 400 characters:

summary: A 3/2-Collatz step on a mixed with Euclid-like subtractions on a second number b; it halts exactly at b = 1 with a = 0 mod 4. The map is proved in Lean for every even a (the only kind the run meets), non-halting is reduced in Lean to the map's orbit, and 10^5 passes are checked (probviously non-halting, P(halt) ~ 2/a).
family: 3/2-Collatz on a with a Euclid-like second number b; halts at b = 1
